procedure: Listen to the teacher’s introduction and example of a simple system.
Work in pairs and choose a system to design.
Define the objective of the chosen system.
Use diagramming software to create a system prototype or diagram.
Present the design to the class and take part in the review and feedback session.
Use the feedback to refine the design.
aim: To apply the principles of system design by defining a system’s objective, components, interactions and environment, and creating a prototype or diagram.

viva.question: What is a system?
viva.answer: A set of interacting components working together to achieve an objective.

viva.question: What is the objective of a system?
viva.answer: The goal or purpose the system is designed to achieve.

viva.question: What are system components?
viva.answer: The parts that make up a system.

viva.question: What do interactions describe?
viva.answer: How the components of a system relate to or work with one another.

viva.question: What is a system’s environment?
viva.answer: The surroundings and external factors that can affect or interact with the system.

viva.question: Why is feedback useful when designing a system?
viva.answer: It helps identify improvements and refine the design.

apparatus: Computer or tablet with diagramming software
diagram: Draw a system diagram and label the system name, objective, components, interactions between components, and environment.
title: Designing a Simple System
precautions: Define the system’s objective clearly before drawing the diagram.
Include the main components needed to achieve the objective.
Show interactions between components clearly and accurately.
Label the system and its environment so the diagram is easy to understand.
Use the computer or tablet carefully and save the work.
result: A system prototype or diagram was created showing its objective, components, interactions and environment. Feedback was used to refine the design.
